content:
There will be a meeting at IPAM from February 13-17 on machine assisted proofs:
https://www.ipam.ucla.edu/programs/workshops/machine-assisted-proofs/
It should be a really interesting gathering, and it features a number of members of the Lean community among the speakers. The workshop is open to general participants, either in person or remote.
In-person attendance will be limited by the size of the room and Terry Tao has just announced the meeting on his blog, so if you are interested in attending in person, don't wait too long.
Apparently all videos got uploaded the same day to https://www.youtube.com/@IPAMUCLA. Kudos to IPAM!

Things are working incredibly smoothly at IPAM. Since 2020 I've participated in countless remote and hybrid events and I've never seen three days of perfectly smooth and relaxed technical operation as what I've witness here. And indeed videos are uploaded twice a day to YouTube.

I was astonished to see the auto-informalization program written in Lean by you and Kyle Miller; I'd been thinking of developing and then selling a video game that enables a player to read/write informal proofs in controlled natural languages, which are automatically translated from/into formal proofs. (Currently I don't know how to do this because I still have loads of things to learn. I'm not even a programmer yet.)
And as a remote attendee I echo this compliment to the organizers, and strongly recommend Patrick's great talk on Youtube here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tp_h3vzkObo

Hi @Jason Rute, thanks for the interesting talk at IPAM Workshop. You mentioned that there is a better way to extract the data for proof search using the tool that Mario made. Can you please share the link to that tool? Thanks!

@Ayush Agrawal I don’t know if anyone has directly used @Mario Carneiro Lean 3 AST extractor tool for this, but it should be possible. Here is a set of links to existing tools for machine learning research in Lean (at the time of the post). #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > What is the AMI project's vision for AI in Lean?
#general > AST export for lean 3 is where Mario introduced the tool.
